I was able to reproduce with Jamsers' scene without changing anything other than adding the lightmapGI node and hitting bake.

> [Calinou](https://github.com/Calinou) Can you run some tests and get a feel for the bake time increase that results from decreasing `rendering/lightmapping/bake_performance/region_size` and `rendering/lightmapping/bake_performance/max_rays_per_pass`? IMO we should just reduce them to the lowest value we can without increasing the bake size significantly. Can you try to find out what those values would be?

OK, I've started doing tests and will post results here shortly.

General observations:

- Changing **Max Rays per Pass** up or down does not change bake times noticeably.

- Increasing **Region Size** to 1024 can reduce bake times significantly if you have enough memory and a fast enough GPU to avoid TDRs (or an OS that doesn't have a concept of TDRs... i.e. anything that's not Windows).
  - If we change the default region size to fix this issue, we may want to do so with a `windows` feature tag to avoid negatively impacting bake times on other platforms.
  - Going above 1024 doesn't noticeably improve bake times, at least in this project. It might be able to do so in larger scenes, provided you have enough VRAM.

- **Region Size** is rounded up to the nearest power of 2, but the project settings allow any integer value. We should fix this so you can't use values that *look* different but are actually the same, or make non-power-of-two values functional.
  - A way to fix this without breaking compatibility is to make use of `PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM` with numbered indices for each item, so that existing values are read as-is.

Not really because the crash doesn't originate in Godot. It comes from the OS thinking that Godot might be frozen. To catch the error you would need to first solve the [Halting problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halting_problem)
@Calinou Can you make a PR setting the default value for max_rays to 4?

> [@Calinou](https://github.com/Calinou?rgh-link-date=2025-02-05T21%3A42%3A13.000Z) Can you make a PR setting the default value for max_rays to 4? Done: - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102477

The error still happens. Using `max_rays` to 4 fixes the issue for low texel resolution or low quality. But using `high` quality (which assumes more rays) the error still happens. 

Is there a way to prevent full utilization of the GPU during bake? To ensure this error does't happen? Another solution?

I answered on the chat as well, but copying here for posterity

Based on your stack trace, that is actually a different crash

The stack trace points to the direct lighting pass crashing. Which makes sense since direct lighting doesn't use `rendering/lightmapping/bake_performance/max_rays_per_pass`
It uses:
`rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/low_quality_ray_count`
`rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/medium_quality_ray_count`
`rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/high_quality_ray_count`
or
`rendering/lightmapping/bake_quality/ultra_quality_ray_count`

depending on the quality setting. It should be a pretty simple fix, we just need to add support for doing multiple passes for direct light baking, the same as what we have already for indirect lighting

In that case I will create new Issue for this. Thanks

Edit: Link https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106975
